epic.title: epic-418-followon — make agents use the MCP door instead of the CLI
epic.intent_and_why: Agents drive their spines through the MCP door rather than the CLI, with per-task spine ownership and an identity that survives an agent dropping off and respawning. Cross-platform usability matters but is explicitly not this round's problem.

definition_of_done: An agent dispatched through run_crew.py drives its own spine through the door, measured from its own call record: door calls > 0 and CLI engine invocations == 0.
A respawned agent on the same assignment resumes its lease instead of force-claiming it.

good_enough.mandatory_quality: Every claim about what happened brings its evidence; a control must reproduce the defect before a fix is believed.
good_enough.sufficient_evidence: Measured from the driving agent's own call record, never from the engine's refusals counter.
good_enough.appetite: One bounded wave; keep out the easy failures rather than making it foolproof.

hard_constraints: docs/agents/* edits are a human's call
No merge or push to main while the human is AFK
Planning makes no direct gh or network mutation
fixed_decisions: The lease keys on the assignment, not the process instance
Identity is derived from the spine's own work_id, never hand-typed
The CLI door stays as a fallback; F is additive

current_wave.objective: Make the door launchable where the owner works (PR #555), on the assumption that Windows launch was the blocker on adoption.
exit_criteria: The door launches from a fresh install on Windows and POSIX, proven in CI

issues.title: Make the MCP door launch where python3 is not a command
issues.desired_outcome: The door launches from a fresh install on both platforms.
issues.useful_now: It was believed to be the blocker on adoption.
issues.acceptance_or_falsification_evidence: Green CI on windows-latest plus a cold review.
issues.implementation_latitude: Choose the interpreter resolution; no literal interpreter in the shipped path.
hard_constraints_no_gos: No user-scope writes under a project-scope flag
local_unknowns: Whether --wire-mcp writes only where the caller named

wave_forecast.why_likely: It was gated on a settled verb contract and a launchable door
entry_conditions: The door launches from a fresh install on Windows and POSIX

uncertainty_register.affects: Whether instruction edits are worth further investment
uncertainty_register.settle_by: A measurement whose arms load a corpus containing the edits
uncertainty_register.current_evidence: All three F2 arms loaded a pre-edit corpus; arm 3 found the door via ToolSearch, not via any instruction
uncertainty_register.next_probe: Re-measure once a launchable, correctly-bound door exists

parked_possibilities: Removing the CLI fallback for agents entirely (#559)

wave_evidence.claim: The MCP door does not work in this environment
wave_evidence.expected: The door fails to launch or fails to serve here
wave_evidence.observed: FALSIFIED. `claude mcp list` reports the spine server Connected, all 7 tools are present in an interactive session, and a direct JSON-RPC handshake with SPINE_FILE set returns this epic's own execute gate and live lease. The server is sound.
wave_evidence.source: claude mcp list; direct initialize + tools/call handshake against scripts/mcp_spine_server.py, 2026-08-10

wave_evidence.claim: Windows launch (#553) is the blocker on door adoption
wave_evidence.expected: Fixing the launch line unblocks agents using the door
wave_evidence.observed: FALSIFIED for this host. The door launches fine here and still cannot be used, because it binds to examples/mcp-interactive-demo/spine.json. Windows launch is a real and separate defect.
wave_evidence.source: spine_status through the approved door returned the demo's gate g1, not this epic's execute step

wave_evidence.claim: Nothing in any shipped launch path binds the door to the caller's spine
wave_evidence.expected: Some shipped script sets SPINE_FILE per dispatch
wave_evidence.observed: CONFIRMED. `grep -rln SPINE_FILE scripts/` returns exactly one file, mcp_spine_server.py, which only reads it. run_crew.py has zero MCP references. The only places it has ever been set are three throwaway measurement scripts under commander-f2/evidence/g4b/run_arm*.sh.
wave_evidence.source: grep over scripts/; read of run_crew.py crew_env() at line 388

wave_evidence.claim: In-session subagents cannot own a spine binding, so per-task binding is impossible
wave_evidence.expected: Every dispatched agent inherits the parent's bound spine
wave_evidence.observed: FALSIFIED as stated. It holds only for in-session Agent-tool subagents (F2 arms 1 and 2: 0 door calls against 21 and 20 CLI). run_crew.py spawns crew as separate `claude -p` processes whose environment is built by crew_env(), so each could bind its own spine.

wave_evidence.claim: Lease identity is stable across a respawn
wave_evidence.expected: A resumed agent re-claims the same identity idempotently
wave_evidence.observed: FALSIFIED. Four live spines in this epic carry four different ad-hoc identities: a session UUID (admiral), None/never-claimed (commander-f2 execute.json), and hand-typed `g2-implement-session` and `g4a-implement-session`. This spine's own init imperative asks for the stable `admiral-epic-418-followon`; two successive sessions typed UUIDs instead.
wave_evidence.source: read of the four spine files' engine_session and work_id fields, 2026-08-10

wave_evidence.claim: The mechanism for respawn-safe ownership must be built from scratch
wave_evidence.observed: FALSIFIED. run_crew.py::session_name already mints the deterministic nesting-aware name constellation/<work-id>/<gate>/<role>/attempt-<n>, and checklist_engine.py::claim already gives idempotent same-id resume, refusal on a different active id, force-with-reason takeover recording previous_session_id, and staleness self-yield. The two halves were never connected.
wave_evidence.source: read of run_crew.py lines 148-206 and checklist_engine.py claim() lines 960-1018

discrepancies.signal: The door is connected and correct but binds to the demo example spine, because nothing in any shipped launch path sets SPINE_FILE
discrepancies.evidence: spine_status through the approved door returned the demo's gate g1; grep -rln SPINE_FILE scripts/ returns only the server that reads it
discrepancies.reason: It does not block #555's own exit criterion — that wave could pass on its own terms and still leave adoption impossible. It invalidates the decomposition, because the wave was aimed at the wrong axis

discrepancies.signal: The planned wave targets Windows launch (#555), which is not what blocks adoption
discrepancies.evidence: The door launches correctly on this host and is still unusable; #421's entry condition was written against the launch axis
discrepancies.reason: The decomposition was built on a falsified premise about which defect gates adoption

discrepancies.signal: Lease identity is hand-typed and has drifted four times in this epic, so a respawn cannot resume its own assignment
discrepancies.evidence: Four spines, four conventions; this spine's own imperative asks for a stable id that two sessions overrode with UUIDs
discrepancies.reason: The human specified respawn-safe identity as a from-the-beginning requirement, so it belongs in the current wave rather than the forecast

discrepancies.signal: Windows launch remains a genuine defect with a promising but unverified fix parked on PR #555 at 6b947546
discrepancies.evidence: CI green on that commit (run 31405772388, windows-latest); the suite never completed under supervision and no cold reviewer has seen it
discrepancies.reason: Real, but not on the path to this round's goal, and the human accepted being broken on Windows for now

discrepancies.signal: The claim that dispatched agents must inherit the parent's bound spine
discrepancies.evidence: run_crew.py spawns separate claude processes with an environment built by crew_env(); only in-session Agent-tool subagents share the parent's servers
discrepancies.reason: The evidence falsified it as a general constraint
